messages:
carla: Quick thought experiment: implement an "on-spill" reservation where we only allocate a tenant reserve when an enqueue would push the merge window past the spill threshold. Aim: reduce idle reserved headroom for many tiny requests. Want safety + ops checks.

nate: sounds promising. main risks i see: 1) racey reservation creation, 2) cold kernel/kv warmup causing p99 spikes when reserve is first created.

yuna: agree. we should require a single atomic createIfAbsent that returns a stable reservation id or failure. that avoids double-counting if two enqueues race.

carla: exactly. admission remains an optimistic admit (gives credit tokens) but does NOT consume ledger until enqueue hits spill. if createIfAbsent fails we return ErrReserveCreationFailed and run fallback eviction path.

nate: what about soft vs hard semantics? if we make the new reservation hard immediately we can starve others. soft-first with a short protect TTL seems safer. promote to hard on commit heartbeat.

yuna: promotion window needs to be tuned per SLO. suggest defaults: soft_protect_ms=40, promote_after_ms=20, promote_backoff=150ms. track promotion_fail_rate metric.

carla: sketching pseudocode:
```go
// returns (reservationID, ok)
func ensureOnSpillReserve(batchWindow, tenant, tokens) (string, bool) {
  if batch.size+tokens <= spillThreshold { return "", true }
  id := ledger.CASCreateIfAbsent(key, tokens) // atomic
  if id == "" { return "", false }
  ledger.SetSoftProtect(id, softProtectMs)
  return id, true
}
```

nate: ops signals: reserve_create_count, reserve_create_latency, promotion_latency, promotion_fail_rate, headroom_utilization, eviction_count. also per-tenant reserve_create_rate to avoid noisy tenants spamming creates.

yuna: we need backstops: (1) per-tenant create rate limit; (2) circuit-breaker: if promotion_fail_rate > X% for a tenant, pin that tenant to eager reserves or a reserved lane; (3) exponential backoff on retries after eviction to avoid thrash.

carla: agree. also add a reconciler job to reap leaked soft protections on host crash and detect phantom reservations. ledger must be durable across coordinator restarts.

nate: testing plan: local microbench, then canary with two slices: latency-sensitive (p95 target 30ms) and cost-sensitive. measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/request, reserve_promotion_fail_rate.

yuna: admission API change note: callers must handle ErrReserveCreationFailed and ErrPreemptedByEviction. provide recommended client retry/backoff. document optimistic admit semantics clearly.

infra-bot: scheduled: canary-latebind start=1770000100 duration=45m

carla: i'll draft a short RFC with invariants (idempotent CAS, no leaked credits on failure, optimistic admit semantics), metrics, config knobs, and backstop rules. will tag for review. thanks for quick feedback.
